FAKE TEST DOCUMENT - NOT A REAL REGULATION
Fictional Data Protection Guidelines for Unit Tests
This text was written for CompliBot's test-suite. It imitates the layout of
Singapore advisory guidelines but none of its content is real law or guidance.

FAKE TEST DOCUMENT - NOT A REAL REGULATION
1 INTRODUCTION
1.1 These fictional guidelines explain how an imaginary organisation should
treat personal data. They exist only to test clause-aware chunking.
2 THE CONSENT OBLIGATION
2.1 An organisation must obtain the consent of an individual before collecting,
using or disclosing the individual's personal data for a purpose, unless an
exception applies.
2.2 Consent must be informed. The organisation should notify the individual of
the purposes for which the personal data will be collected, used or disclosed,
and the notification should be made on or before collection.
2.3 An individual may withdraw consent at any time by giving reasonable notice.
The organisation must stop collecting, using or disclosing the personal data
within 10 business days of receiving the withdrawal notice.

---page---
FAKE TEST DOCUMENT - NOT A REAL REGULATION
3 THE PROTECTION OBLIGATION
3.1 Security Arrangements
3.1.1 An organisation must protect personal data in its possession by making
reasonable security arrangements to prevent unauthorised access, collection,
use, disclosure, copying or modification.
3.1.2 Encryption should be applied to personal data stored on portable devices
such as laptops and USB drives. The organisation should also maintain an
access log reviewed at least quarterly. Fees increased by
2.5 per cent in the fictional example year, which must not be read as a clause.
4 THE RETENTION LIMITATION OBLIGATION
4.1 An organisation should cease to retain personal data as soon as the purpose
for which it was collected is no longer being served by retention.
4.2 Personal data that is no longer needed should be anonymised or securely
destroyed within 30 days.
